info.name: DMS - Distributor Management System
info.description:
# DMS — Distributor Management System

A B2B supply-chain backend for FMCG and pharmaceutical distributors. Field Sales
Representatives place credit orders on behalf of retail shops; the system enforces
per-shop credit limits, deducts branch inventory atomically, and settles through bKash.

**This is not e-commerce.** Retailers never log in — they are business records. The SR is
the only actor who creates an order, and staff accounts are created by an admin or a
branch manager, never by public signup.

## Base URL

Set the `baseUrl` variable. Locally that is `http://localhost:5000/api/v1`.

## Authentication

All protected routes use **Bearer tokens**. The collection sends `{{accessToken}}`
automatically — run **Auth → Login**, copy `data.accessToken` from the response into the
`accessToken` collection variable, and every other request is authorised.

Access tokens last 15 minutes; refresh tokens last 7 days and are set as an httpOnly
cookie. `POST /auth/logout` and a password reset both raise the account's token version,
which revokes every token already issued — including copies on other devices.

## Roles

| Role | Branch | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | none | Everything, across all branches |
| `BRANCH_MANAGER` | required | Their own branch only — 403 on any other |
| `FIELD_SR` | required | Creates orders; sees only their own |

## Response format

Every endpoint answers in one shape. Success:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Operation successful", "data": {} }
```

Paginated endpoints add `meta`: `{ "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 45, "totalPage": 5 }`.

Failure:

```json
{ "success": false, "message": "Validation failed", "errors": [{ "path": "email", "message": "Invalid email" }] }
```

`GET /orders/:id/invoice` is the one exception — it returns `application/pdf`.

## Status codes

| Code | Means |
|---|---|
| 400 | Validation failed, or the request is not valid for the current state |
| 401 | Missing, expired or revoked token |
| 403 | Authenticated, but this role or branch may not do it |
| 404 | No such record, or not visible to this role |
| 409 | Conflicts with another in-flight change — safe to retry |
| 429 | Rate limited: 100 requests / 15 min globally, 5 / 15 min on auth |
| 503 | An optional service (SMTP, Cloudinary, bKash) is not configured |

## Optional services

Redis, SMTP, Cloudinary and bKash are all optional. The API boots and serves without any
of them — only the routes that need one return 503, and Redis degrades silently. Postgres
is the only hard requirement.

request.description: Requires a valid access token. Revokes all access and refresh sessions for this staff account.

item.description:
Registration is **two steps**. `POST /auth/register` is called by an admin or branch
manager, stages the account in Redis for five minutes and emails a six-digit code — it
returns **202** and no tokens. `POST /auth/verify-email` consumes the code, creates the
user and returns the session.

Keeping the pending signup out of Postgres means an abandoned registration leaves nothing
behind: no half-built row holding the email address, and no cleanup job.

Codes are single use, expire in five minutes and allow five attempts. `forgot-password`
answers identically whether or not the account exists, so it cannot be used to discover
which addresses are registered.

`<value>:deleted:<id>`, so the address can be reused. It refuses to remove your own
account or the last remaining super admin.

item.description:
The shared SKU catalogue, priced once globally. Listing is cached in Redis for
five minutes and the cache is invalidated on every write.

Deletion is soft and also appends `:deleted:<id>` to the SKU, so the code can be reused
by a new product without tripping the unique index.

item.name: Inventory

request.description: Atomic increment or conditional decrement. Stock can never go below zero, and concurrent adjustments cannot lose one another.
A manager/SR sees only their own branch; SUPER_ADMIN sees all and may pass ?branchId=.

item.description:
Stock is held per branch and product. A branch manager and an SR only ever see
their own branch; a super admin can look across branches and narrow with `?branchId=`.

Adjustments are atomic increments and conditional decrements, so two concurrent
adjustments cannot lose one another or take stock below zero.

request.description: Responds with application/pdf rather than the usual JSON envelope. Role-scoped exactly like Get Order By Id.
Sends the same PDF as an attachment to retailers.email. Returns 400 if that retailer has no email on file, and 503 if SMTP is not configured.

item.description:
The core workflow. `POST /orders` runs in one transaction: prices come from the
product table so a client cannot dictate what it pays, credit is reserved by a conditional
update, and stock is decremented conditionally. Any failure rolls all of it back.

Status follows a fixed machine: `PENDING → APPROVED → DISPATCHED → DELIVERED`, with
`CANCELLED` reachable from `PENDING` and `APPROVED` only. Cancelling returns the stock
and reverses the credit, and is refused while a payment is pending or settled.

item.name: Payment

request.description: Creates a bKash checkout and returns `bkashURL`. Returns 409 if a payment is already pending for this order.

response.name: 403 — not your order

originalRequest.description: Creates a bKash checkout and returns `bkashURL`. Returns 409 if a payment is already pending for this order.

request.description: Where bKash returns the customer browser. The callback alone is never trusted — the server calls execute to confirm before crediting.

The GET form of the callback, which is how bKash returns the customer browser after checkout. Same verification as the POST form: the query string alone is never trusted, so the server calls execute to confirm the payment before crediting anything.
A single payment with its order summary, for status tracking.

Reverses a settled payment through bKash and puts the money back on the retailer account: paidAmount comes down, dueBalance goes back up, and the payment moves to REFUNDED.

Deliberately its own endpoint rather than a side effect of cancelling an order — returning money is a decision someone makes, so it is role-gated and audited, and `reason` is required.

Only a payment that actually settled can be refunded; bKash identifies the movement by the trxID that only exists once execute confirmed it. Once refunded, the order becomes cancellable.

item.description:
bKash tokenized checkout. `initiate` creates a gateway payment and returns a
`bkashURL` for the browser; the callback is never trusted on its own, so the server calls
bKash's execute endpoint to confirm before crediting anything.

Repeated initiation is refused with **409** while a payment is already pending, which is
what stops a retailer being charged twice for one order.

A settled payment can be reversed with `POST /payments/:id/refund`. That is what makes a paid order cancellable: refund first, then cancel. FAILED and REFUNDED are both settled outcomes and neither blocks cancellation.
